glance.label: Main Idea
glance.html: The LORD closes His instructions for the tabernacle by filling Bezalel with His Spirit and appointing Aholiab and skilled workers to build it, by giving the Sabbath as the sign that He sanctifies His people, and by handing Moses the tablets written with the finger of God.

glance.label: Setting
glance.html: Exodus 31 ends the instructions Moses received on Sinai (24:18–31:18), just before the people below make the golden calf (32:1).

glance.label: Chapter Outline
glance.html:
• Exodus 31:1–11 — God Fills Bezalel and Appoints Aholiab for the Work

  • Exodus 31:12–17 — The Sabbath as the Sign That the LORD Sanctifies Israel

  • Exodus 31:18 — The Tablets Written with the Finger of God

glance.label: Key Verse
glance.html: “Surely My Sabbaths you shall keep, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” (Exodus 31:13)

cards.title: The Heart of the Chapter
cards.html:
God has given the pattern; now He provides the people to build it. “See, I have called by name Bezalel” (31:2), He says, and He has filled him “with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship” (31:3). The first person in Scripture said to be filled with God’s Spirit is a craftsman. God gives Bezalel skill in metal, stone, and wood, appoints Aholiab to work beside him, and puts wisdom in the hearts of all the skilled workers. Their gifts serve one purpose: to make everything exactly as God commanded for His dwelling.

Then God gives the Sabbath as a sign, “that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you” (31:13). Rest is part of Israel’s identity as God’s holy people, rooted in His own rest after creation, when “on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed” (31:17). Under Israel’s covenant, profaning the Sabbath was a capital offense, a measure of how seriously God took it. Finally the LORD gives Moses two tablets of stone, “written with the finger of God” (31:18), His own covenant words in His own hand.

cards.title: Chapter Sections
cards.html:
Exodus 31:1–11 — God Fills Bezalel and Appoints Aholiab for the Work

The LORD calls Bezalel of Judah by name and fills him with His Spirit, giving him wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of skill. He appoints Aholiab of Dan to work with him and gives wisdom to all the skilled workers so they can make the tabernacle, its furnishings, the priests’ garments, the oil, and the incense exactly as commanded.

Exodus 31:12–17 — The Sabbath as the Sign That the LORD Sanctifies Israel

The LORD tells Israel to keep His Sabbaths as a sign between Him and them that He is the LORD who makes them holy. Under Israel’s covenant anyone who profanes the day by working is to be put to death, for the Sabbath is a lasting sign rooted in God’s own rest after creation.

Exodus 31:18 — The Tablets Written with the Finger of God

When the LORD finishes speaking with Moses on Sinai, He gives him the two tablets of the Testimony. They are stone tablets written with the finger of God.

cards.title: Why This Chapter Matters
cards.html:
Exodus 31 shows that the Holy Spirit equips God’s people for every kind of work He calls them to, including skilled work with their hands. Bezalel’s artistry was a gift of the Spirit, given to serve God’s dwelling. In Christ, believers are being built together into a dwelling of God in the Spirit (Ephesians 2:22).

The chapter also places rest at the close of all the work instructions. The God who equips His people to work also calls them to stop and rest, and in that rest they remember that He is the One who makes them holy. Jesus, Lord of the Sabbath, calls the weary to find rest in Him (Matthew 11:28–30), and believers are called to a deliberate weekly rhythm of ceasing to enjoy and worship Him.

cards.title: Key Themes to Watch For
cards.html:
Called by name. God personally chooses Bezalel for the work (31:2).

Filled with the Spirit for skill. The Spirit of God gives wisdom and craftsmanship for building His dwelling (31:3–6).

Everything as commanded. The workers make all that God commanded, from the ark to the incense (31:6–11).

The Sabbath sign. The Sabbath marks Israel as the people the LORD sanctifies (31:13–17).

God’s written word. The tablets are written with the finger of God (31:18).

cards.title: Key Words & Concepts
cards.html:
Bezalel (31:2). A craftsman from Judah whom God filled with His Spirit to lead the building of the tabernacle.

Aholiab (31:6). A craftsman from Dan whom God appointed to work alongside Bezalel.

Sign (31:13). A visible mark of a relationship. The Sabbath showed that Israel belonged to the LORD who made them holy.

Sanctifies (31:13). Makes holy and sets apart for Himself.

Finger of God (31:18). An expression for God’s direct authorship. The tablets carried His own covenant words with His full authority.

focus: Exodus 31 closes the LORD’s instructions for the tabernacle by naming Bezalel, whom He fills with His Spirit, and Aholiab, whom He appoints to work with him, to carry out everything He has commanded. He then gives the Sabbath as the sign that He sanctifies His people and hands Moses the two tablets of the Testimony written with the finger of God.

sections.title: God Fills Bezalel and Appoints Aholiab for the Work
sections.summary: The LORD calls Bezalel of Judah by name and fills him “with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship” (Exodus 31:3). He appoints Aholiab of Dan with him and puts wisdom in the hearts of all the skilled artisans, so that they may make the tabernacle, its furnishings, the priestly garments, the oil, and the incense, just as He commanded.

sections.title: The Sabbath as the Sign That the LORD Sanctifies Israel
sections.summary: The LORD commands Israel to keep His Sabbaths, “for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you” (Exodus 31:13). Whoever profanes it by working is to be put to death, for the Sabbath is a perpetual covenant rooted in the LORD’s rest after creating the heavens and the earth.

sections.title: The Tablets Written with the Finger of God
sections.summary: When the LORD finishes speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gives him two tablets of the Testimony. They are tablets of stone, “written with the finger of God” (Exodus 31:18).

1.brief: The LORD speaks to Moses. The instructions now turn to the workers who will build the sanctuary.
1.explain:
“Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:”

God has described what is to be made. Now He names who will make it.

2.brief: God says, “See, I have called by name Bezalel,” son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah. God personally chooses the chief craftsman.
2.explain:
“See, I have called by name Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.”

God says, “I have called by name Bezalel.” God personally chooses the chief craftsman. Bezalel’s grandfather may be the Hur who held up Moses’ hands (17:10–12), though this is not certain.
2.notes: The name Bezalel means in the shadow of God.

3.brief: God has filled Bezalel “with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship.” The Spirit of God equips Bezalel for skilled work.
3.explain:
“And I have filled him with the Spirit of God,”

God has “filled him with the Spirit of God.” This is the first time Scripture says someone is filled with the Spirit of God. The Spirit equips Bezalel for the work God has given.

“in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,”

The Spirit gives “wisdom,” “understanding,” “knowledge,” and skill in “all manner of workmanship.” Artistic and practical ability can be the gift of God’s Spirit when it serves His purpose.

4.brief: Bezalel is gifted to design artistic works and to work in gold, silver, and bronze. His skill covers every kind of metalwork.
4.explain:
“to design artistic works, to work in gold, in silver, in bronze,”

Bezalel can “design” and work in every metal. His skill covers every kind of metalwork.

5.brief: Bezalel is also skilled in cutting jewels, carving wood, and all kinds of workmanship. The Spirit equips him for the full range of the work.
5.explain:
“in cutting jewels for setting, in carving wood, and to work in all manner of workmanship.”

He can also cut stones and carve wood. The Spirit equips him for the full range of the work.

6.brief: God has appointed Aholiab of the tribe of Dan to work with Bezalel and has put wisdom in the hearts of all the gifted artisans to make all God commanded. God provides a partner and a whole team of skilled workers.
6.explain:
“And I, indeed I, have appointed with him Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan;”

God appoints “Aholiab” to work with Bezalel. Bezalel is from Judah, the leading tribe. Aholiab is from Dan, a less prominent tribe. God uses workers from across His people.

“and I have put wisdom in the hearts of all the gifted artisans, that they may make all that I have commanded you:”

God also gives “wisdom” to “all the gifted artisans.” He provides a whole team. Their purpose is to “make all that I have commanded.” God gives skill so that His people can carry out what He commanded.
6.notes: Exodus 35:34–35 adds that God gave both Bezalel and Aholiab the ability to teach others.

7.brief: The artisans will make the tabernacle of meeting, the ark of the Testimony with its mercy seat, and all its furniture. The work begins with the dwelling and its holiest furnishings.
7.explain:
“the tabernacle of meeting, the ark of the Testimony and the mercy seat that is on it, and all the furniture of the tabernacle—”

The list of work begins with the tent and its holiest furnishings.

8.brief: The artisans will make the table and its utensils, the pure gold lampstand, and the altar of incense. The furnishings of the holy place are included.
8.explain:
“the table and its utensils, the pure gold lampstand with all its utensils, the altar of incense,”

The furnishings of the holy place follow.

9.brief: The artisans will make the altar of burnt offering with its utensils and the laver and its base. The courtyard furnishings are included.
9.explain:
“the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the laver and its base—”

The courtyard furnishings are included.

10.brief: The artisans will make the garments of ministry, the holy garments for Aaron and for his sons. The priestly clothing is part of the work.
10.explain:
“the garments of ministry, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister as priests,”

The priestly clothing is part of the work.

11.brief: The artisans will make the anointing oil and sweet incense, and “According to all that I have commanded you they shall do.” Everything must be done according to God’s instructions.
11.explain:
“and the anointing oil and sweet incense for the holy place.”

The oil and incense complete the list.

“According to all that I have commanded you they shall do.”

Everything must be done “according to all that I have commanded.” The Spirit’s gifts serve God’s commands, not the artisans’ own designs.

12.brief: The LORD speaks to Moses. The final instruction on the mountain concerns the Sabbath.
12.explain:
“And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,”

The last instruction on the mountain concerns the Sabbath.

13.brief: Israel must keep God’s Sabbaths, “for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.” The Sabbath marks Israel as the people God makes holy.
13.explain:
“Speak also to the children of Israel, saying: ‘Surely My Sabbaths you shall keep,”

God calls them “My Sabbaths.” Even while building the sanctuary, Israel must keep them. The work on God’s house does not override God’s rest (35:1–3).

“for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations,”

The Sabbath is “a sign” of the covenant between God and Israel, as the rainbow was for Noah (Genesis 9:12–13) and circumcision for Abraham (Genesis 17:11).

“that you may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you.”

God makes His people holy. The Sabbath marks Israel as the people God makes holy.

14.brief: The Sabbath is holy, and anyone who profanes it by working shall surely be put to death and cut off from his people. Under Israel’s covenant, breaking the Sabbath is a grave offense.
14.explain:
“You shall keep the Sabbath, therefore, for it is holy to you.”

The Sabbath is “holy,” set apart.

“Everyone who profanes it shall surely be put to death; for whoever does any work on it, that person shall be cut off from among his people.”

Under Israel’s covenant, breaking the Sabbath carried the death penalty (compare Numbers 15:32–36). This sanction belonged to the old covenant as a sign of Israel’s special relationship with God.

15.brief: Work is done for six days, but the seventh is “the Sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD,” and whoever works on it shall be put to death. The penalty is repeated to stress the Sabbath’s holiness.
15.explain:
“Work shall be done for six days, but the seventh is the Sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD.”

The pattern is six days of work and “the Sabbath of rest.” The Hebrew phrase is emphatic, a complete rest.

“Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death.”

The penalty is repeated to stress the Sabbath’s holiness.

16.brief: Israel is to keep the Sabbath throughout their generations “as a perpetual covenant.” The Sabbath is a lasting part of Israel’s covenant with God.
16.explain:
“Therefore the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations as a perpetual covenant.”

Israel must keep the Sabbath “as a perpetual covenant.” It is a lasting part of Israel’s covenant with God.

17.brief: The Sabbath is a sign forever, for in six days the LORD made the heavens and earth, “and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.” The Sabbath is rooted in God’s own rest at creation.
17.explain:
“It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever;”

The Sabbath is a lasting sign between God and Israel.

“for in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed.”

The reason is creation. God “rested and was refreshed.” The word refreshed reads literally took breath. God does not grow tired (Isaiah 40:28). The language describes His delight in His finished work. The Sabbath is rooted in God’s own rest at creation. For believers, this rest is found in Jesus, the Lord of the Sabbath (Mark 2:27–28), who gives rest and makes His people holy (Matthew 11:28–30; Hebrews 4:9–10). Believers are called to a deliberate weekly rhythm of resting with Him, with freedom concerning the day (Romans 14:5–6; Colossians 2:16–17).
17.notes: The Sabbath was the sign of the covenant between the LORD and Israel, and the death penalty for breaking it (31:14–15) belonged to Israel’s covenant setting as a nation under God.

18.brief: When God finishes speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gives him the two tablets of the Testimony, “written with the finger of God.” The instructions on the mountain end with God’s own written covenant in Moses’ hands.
18.explain:
“And when He had made an end of speaking with him on Mount Sinai,”

God has finished speaking with Moses on the mountain. The instructions that began in 25:1 are complete.

“He gave Moses two tablets of the Testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.”

God gives Moses “two tablets of the Testimony,” written “with the finger of God.” The covenant law comes from God Himself. Moses will soon break these tablets when he sees the golden calf (32:19).
